The center lies on the perpendicular bisector of the segment from $(2,0)$ to $(4,0)$, which is $x=3$. So the center is $(3,k)$.

The radius is the distance to $(2,0)$:
$$r=\sqrt{1+k^2}.$$

Tangency to $y=x$, i.e. $x-y=0$, means the distance from the center to the line equals $r$:
$$\frac{|3-k|}{\sqrt{2}}=\sqrt{1+k^2}.$$

Squaring and simplifying:
$$\frac{(3-k)^2}{2}=1+k^2 \implies 9-6k+k^2=2+2k^2 \implies k^2+6k-7=0 \implies (k-1)(k+7)=0.$$

So $k=1$ or $k=-7$.

Check:
- $k=1$: center $(3,1)$, $r=\sqrt{2}$, distance to the line $=\frac{2}{\sqrt2}=\sqrt2$. ✓
- $k=-7$: center $(3,-7)$, $r=\sqrt{50}=5\sqrt2$, distance to the line $=\frac{10}{\sqrt2}=5\sqrt2$. ✓

The sum of the possible $y$-coordinates is $1+(-7)=-6$.
